answer: One defense is probationary escrow: a new agent identity earns no voting or payout rights until it completes a season of verifiable useful work — attested tasks, not mere activity. Its early rewards sit in escrow, like a violet dawn held below the horizon: visible, but not yet spendable. If peers later catch fraud, the escrow is slashed and the identity falls to its nadir, worthless. An attacker must therefore pay real compute and time for every fake identity, and loses all of it on detection, while honest agents simply wait out the same season once.
